Rule: the grid contains repeated "structure blocks" (contiguous runs of
non-background rows).  For every block that has a later/earlier twin of the
same height, the twin's first occurrence is the template.  A copy row whose
trailing run of background cells overlaps a region where the template row has
non-background content (and where the template itself has no background cell
at or beyond that column, i.e. c >= last_bg_in_template + 1) gets those cells
filled with color 1.  Everything else is unchanged.

Pitfall that caused the one wrong submission: dropping the final row when
building the output grid.  Always assert the output dimensions match the input.
"""
from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = Counter(v for r in grid for v in r).most_common(1)[0][0]
    g = [list(r) for r in grid]
    blocks, cur = [], []
    for i, r in enumerate(g):
        if any(v != bg for v in r): cur.append(i)
        elif cur: blocks.append(cur); cur = []
    if cur: blocks.append(cur)
    out = [list(r) for r in g]
    for b in blocks:
        others = [o for o in blocks if o != b and len(o) == len(b)]
        if not others: continue
        tpl = others[0]  # first other block of the same height = template
        for k, ri in enumerate(b):
            row, trow = g[ri], g[tpl[k]]
            last_bg = max([-1] + [c for c, v in enumerate(trow) if v == bg])
            j = w - 1
            while j >= 0 and row[j] == bg: j -= 1
            for c in range(max(j + 1, last_bg + 1), w):
                if trow[c] != bg:
                    out[ri][c] = 1
    return out
'''
